project: aza3, head-only functional interpretation of Azami + EAzami + GloBI without modifying frozen chapters
focal_question: When do interacting capitulum structures evolve together, independently, or compensatorily, as a function of pollinator/seed-feeder/parasitoid access and abiotic reproductive protection?
scientific_headline_boundary: Hypotheses and data-informed interface candidates. No new field-selection, causal mechanical spine, genetic coevolution or adaptation evidence is claimed.

modules.name: capitulum_presentation_angle
modules.measurement: gravity-referenced anthesis angle and time-resolved angle, plus sham treatment contrast
cannot_infer: final adaptive value without viable achenes

modules.name: whole_head_shape_and_floret_packing
modules.measurement: diameter, true 3D length/width, floret density and pollen release stage; head rank
functional_routes: visual detection range and encounter area
number of seed prey units and resource size
cannot_infer: plant-level head number is not individual head morphology

modules.name: floral_colour_UV_display
modules.measurement: calibrated pigment visible/UV, display appearance; nectar/reward independently
cannot_infer: pigment genetically reactivated from leaf RNA

modules.name: involucral_phyllary_posture_and_access_gaps
modules.measurement: direct phyllary angle, bract coverage and validated entrance-gap geometry at bud/anthesis/fruit
modules.azami_data: involucre_form (2D proxy, not botanical phyllary angle)
functional_routes: phyllary coverage of seeds and floret base
cannot_infer: actual thorn length from posture alone

modules.name: involucral_spine_armature
modules.measurement: direct spine length, direction, rigidity and encounter path, independent of posture
functional_routes: may hinder legitimate access or enemy parasitoid probing
cannot_infer: thorn defence selection from projection RV
synchronic evolution of real spines from posture counts

modules.name: stickiness_and_surface_exudates
modules.measurement: verified natural tack/exudate, season-dependent trap surface and reversible effect vs sham
modules.eazami_data: sticky/nonsticky categorical history >=4–5 changes; field permission gate JPN15
functional_routes: deterrence of ants, aphids and some adversaries
may bypass seed predators and pollinators

modules.name: floret_functional_core
modules.measurement: floret maturity, anther/stigma contact, pollen viability, female and where possible male reproduction; final viable achenes
modules.azami_data: visible corolla colour only, not viability

modules.name: capitulum_phenophase_and_reorientation
modules.measurement: repeated same-head bud/anthesis/fruit orientation and exposed entry area
modules.eazami_data: stage labels needed to avoid taxon polymorphism error
functional_routes: switch of access route across ovipositing adults, pollination and parasitoid searching
cannot_infer: ontogenetic change is phylogenetic trait change

comparison_models.question: A shared ecological function requires coupled change in multiple head modules
comparison_models.fitness_signature: joint treatment synergy on prespecified viable-seed scale; positive cross-trait correlational selection in matching guild world
comparison_models.historical_signature: replicated contemporaneous paired transition placements beyond a null conditioned on branch lengths/rates/missingness
comparison_models.limitation: co-transition alone could reflect developmental linkage/common environmental driver

comparison_models.question: Alternative head modules can deliver the same beneficial functional outcome
comparison_models.fitness_signature: two single-module configurations show comparable viable-seed returns despite different route-specific mediators, combined traits give little extra benefit or incur interference cost
comparison_models.historical_signature: conditional/lagged or reciprocal transitions, not necessarily same-branch and possibly zero pooled trait covariance
comparison_models.limitation: non-cochange alone is no evidence of substitution; require causal same-system function and costs

comparison_models.question: Different modules regulate different guilds or phenophases
comparison_models.fitness_signature: trait- and time/guild-specific process effects with final reproductive relevance; cross-term can be near zero
comparison_models.historical_signature: asynchronous transitions may occur independently across lineages
comparison_models.limitation: developmental-stage dependence can mimic historical independence

comparison_models.question: Apparent integration follows developmental/allometric or camera-pose dependencies
comparison_models.fitness_signature: effects unchanged by manipulating ecological partners; no trait-specific mediator or seed fitness change
comparison_models.historical_signature: trait covariance or shared changes persist across ecological regimes
comparison_models.limitation: functional conservation can coexist with developmental correlations

comparison_models.question: Angle, involucre and projections track UV/rain/wind but not animal-access selection
comparison_models.fitness_signature: pollen wetness/viability tracks treatment, animal guild access not mediator
comparison_models.historical_signature: current environment association need not match origin environment
comparison_models.limitation: do not force binary biotic versus abiotic if both routes operate

pairs.functional_hypothesis: head elongation changes visible floret presentation and water interception depending on orientation
pairs.target: time-of-day effective pollen contact, wetness, viable achenes

pairs.functional_hypothesis: joint orientation + appressed/spreading phyllary coverage can shield pollen/ovules or redirect pollinator/ovipositor access
pairs.primary_rival: rain/UV mechanism alone or developmental stage
pairs.target: world/head-centred access + wet pollen + matched viable achenes

pairs.functional_hypothesis: orientation changes mechanical thorn encounter only when guild approach route is world-centred
pairs.target: actual spine geometry x head angle x pollinator/ovipositor/parasitoid access + viable seed

pairs.functional_hypothesis: splayed phyllaries can expand the protective radial thorn perimeter, or posture and spine length act redundantly on the same entry route
pairs.target: entry probability conditional on approach route, plus reproduction

pairs.functional_hypothesis: bract angle positions sticky surfaces away from pollinator corridors and on crawling-insect routes; alternative trap/coverage control
pairs.target: separate pollinator, seed predator, ant/aphid and predatory arthropod channel

pairs.functional_hypothesis: high visibility can raise both legitimate and illegitimate arrivals; accessible thorns may preferentially filter enemies
pairs.primary_rival: shared taxon ecology, photo contrast and geometry correlation
pairs.target: detected arrivals to final effective pollen and damage then filled achenes

pairs.functional_hypothesis: more conspicuous head/displays raise pollinator and egg-laying opportunity; defensive barriers may rescue returns
pairs.primary_rival: larger floret/plant resource makes more seeds even without pollinators
pairs.target: head-level resources separate from plant-level head number, effective contacts and oviposition

pairs.functional_hypothesis: mechanical and sticky barriers may compensate, specialize on different insect guilds, or jointly punish legitimate visitors
pairs.primary_rival: one mechanistic barrier dominates and the rest are correlated ornaments
pairs.target: safe randomized two-attribute cross first; 3-factor only if powered

pairs.functional_hypothesis: earlier enclosed/spiny state excludes seed-feeder oviposition while later exposure permits beneficial parasitoid access without impairing pollination
pairs.primary_rival: parasitoids attack too late to rescue already damaged seeds
pairs.target: same-head staged egg placement, early host killing, tissue damage timing and viable seeds

primary_experimental_contrast.units: independent plant randomization/block, repeated bouts nested within head, not independent
primary_experimental_contrast.treatment: orientation vs sham × reversible externally qualified phyllary/access state vs sham; real-spine arm only after direct calibration and independent safe perturbation
primary_experimental_contrast.baseline: independent pre-treatment guild pressure (legitimate effective pollination, adult seed-feeder oviposition, parasitoid attack opportunities) plus rain/UV/head-rank and phenophase
separate_mechanisms: pre-anthesis or anthesis oviposition/early larval damage
timely parasitoid oviposition and host mortality
ultimate_endpoints: viable filled achenes per focal capitulum
whole-plant viable seed output where measured
primary_experimental_contrast.operator: Delta_OS = W11 - W10 - W01 + W00 on predeclared viable-achene scale; negative does NOT alone distinguish substitution from interference
interpretation_ladder: replicated phylogenetic/population transition dependence beyond null
guardrails: No direct user field manipulations or collection authorized by plan
No inference that RGB brightness is actual UV/pigment
No assumption a bee/butterfly is beneficial or a fly antagonistic without behaviour
No random-vs-adaptive inference from EAzami 0/3 synchronized transitions alone

key_prior_art.meaning: spine removal changes illegitimate but not frequency of legitimate visitor landings; 22% lower filled seeds
nodding shields pollen against rain/UV and improves seed set without known pollinator preference
preferential pollination of white colour morph; colour is not universally just pigment cost
display impacts bumblebee response and seed predation; plant-vs-head levels distinct
sticky inflorescence not universally protective; guild-dependent pathways

Factorial pollinator × herbivore impact already demonstrates nonlinear plant-fitness consequences and a possible route to correlational selection; the authors manipulated interaction agents, not specific capitulum traits.
sequential pollination and seed predation selection is established prior art; novelty must be a distinctive whole-head conditional access architecture

key_prior_art.study: Ohashi, Jurgens and Thomson 2021 Biological Reviews trade-off mitigation
key_prior_art.meaning: Temporal phenotype switching, combinational modifier traits, active exclusion, peak blunting, optima convergence already introduced; these general mechanisms are NOT novel.

key_prior_art.study: 2019 Communications Biology Merianieae 3-D pollinator functional modularity
key_prior_art.meaning: Adaptive floral modularity reorganization and pollinator shift already supported; generic module rearrangement is NOT novel.

key_prior_art.study: Romstock-Volkl 1990 Cirsium heterophyllum tephritid ovipositor refuges
key_prior_art.meaning: Existing capitulum structural refuge for herbivore larvae against parasitoids; the novel issue would be whether whole-head trait coupling changes plant fitness via that tri-trophic route.

new_observed_head_evidence.sample: 1,734 image observations, 42 Cirsium taxon labels, same 18 endpoints and nine constructs, 36 RV pairs
new_observed_head_evidence.statistical_scope: 3,000 taxon bootstraps, 9,999 taxon label shuffles each pair, BH for 36; separate signed taxon and 6-covariate image/geo/climate sensitivity; no phylogenetic null, fitness or botanical thorn

chosen_biological_tests.question: Does more conspicuous flower optical display increase legitimate pollen delivery and adult seed-feeder approaches, and do independently measured armature and phyllary access traits filter the harmful arrival more than legitimate pollinators?
chosen_biological_tests.required_outcome: effective pollen deposition, actual herbivore egg placement, floret damage, early parasitoid access, final viable achene count
chosen_biological_tests.null: Common phylogeny/photos or pigment–microclimate covariance creates association without causal adaptive coupled function
chosen_biological_tests.baseline: Validated visible+UV reflectance and actual physical spine, not image chroma and projection alone

chosen_biological_tests.question: Does head geometry condition the effect of natural orientation on rain/UV protection and diurnal pollinator handling?
chosen_biological_tests.required_outcome: head wetting, pollen viability, hourly effective flower contact, achene fitness
chosen_biological_tests.null: Perspective-based image association or head allometry

chosen_biological_tests.question: Does orienting the same bract-spine structure in world coordinates change the accessibility of aerial ovipositors, legitimate pollinators and early host parasitoids even when evolutionary morphological covariance is weak?
chosen_biological_tests.required_outcome: world-vs-head-centred insect approach vectors, successful access, oviposition and pre-damage parasitism, final seeds
chosen_biological_tests.null: Animals fully align to head-centred coordinates or parasitoids arrive too late to save seeds

chosen_biological_tests.question: Can a head restrict early seed-feeder oviposition yet later expose parasitized larvae to enemy attack via time-varying geometry?
chosen_biological_tests.required_outcome: pre-established host infestation, time-resolved development/trait geometry, realized early killing and seed rescue
chosen_biological_tests.null: Ontogenetic angle change unrelated to enemy interaction and ineffective late parasitism

new_observed_head_evidence.stop_rule: No Nature-level adaptive reconstruction from source-image RV, trait marginal frequency, historical 0/3 co-transitions, GloBI flower visits or numerical simulators. Genetic evolution requires independent measured hereditary transitions, guild regime and corresponding fitness.
